paragraphs: Friend, Job just handed us a whole lesson on what NOT to do when somebody is hurting. He calls his friends "miserable comforters" (Job 16:2), and he says if the roles were switched, he would use his mouth to encourage them, and "the consolation of my lips would bring relief" (Job 16:4-5). When a person is in pain, speeches don't help. Showing up and being kind does.

Here's the part I love, though. Job doesn't pretty up his pain, and he doesn't hand it to his friends. He pours out his tears "to God" (Job 16:20). Even with his spirit broken and the grave waiting, he says, "my hands are free of violence and my prayer is pure" (Job 16:17), and "my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high" (Job 16:19). I think that's what honest prayer looks like: all of the hurt, brought to the One who hears.

So here's your takeaway, baker. When a friend is hurting, be the comforter Job wished he had, short on words and long on kindness. When YOU are hurting, you don't have to say "I'm fine," because you can bring the whole mess to God. Job's story is far from over, and so is yours.
